edges.description: Proposed. TBC1D24 binds ARF6, a small GTPase that regulates exo-endocytosis, and TBC1D24 knockdown alters ARF6 activation; no study has measured ARF6 signalling with the FIME alleles.

Disease-associated TBC1D24 variants behave as loss-of-function alleles, and loss of TBC1D24 impairs presynaptic endocytosis. This edge is inferred for FIME: the synaptic studies used knockdown, knockout and an allelic series of other disease variants, not the FIME alleles.
TBC1D24 overexpression lengthens and branches neurites, and the FIME variants cancel that effect. That ARF6 mediates the effect is the authors' proposal; the assay did not test ARF6 dependence.

Proposed. The discovery paper argues that the neurite defect produces subtle cytoarchitectural changes, below the level of a visible lesion, that make cortical networks hyperexcitable. No tissue observation in patients supports the intermediate step.
Defective vesicle recycling is proposed as a common synaptic mechanism behind the epilepsies of the TBC1D24 spectrum.

nodes.description: Proposed node. TBC1D24 interacts with ARF6, which regulates membrane exo-endocytosis, dendritic branching, spine formation and axonal extension. The discovery paper proposed this pathway as the route from TBC1D24 to brain hyperexcitability; whether the FIME alleles change ARF6 signalling has not been measured.

nodes.description: Symptomatic pharmacologic management of seizures. Seizures in the founding family responded well to treatment, unlike the drug-resistant epilepsy that is common elsewhere in the TBC1D24 spectrum. No specific drug has been shown to be preferred in FIME.

nodes.description: Both TBC1D24 alleles carry missense or in-frame variants (D147H in the TBC domain and A509V in the TLDc domain in the founding family; homozygous E153K or an in-frame 12-bp deletion in later families). The founding alleles lose TBC1D24's neurite-promoting activity in cultured neurons. Partial rather than complete loss of function is inferred from the in-frame nature of the alleles and from the absence of the axon-formation defect in neurons from a mildly affected patient; it has not been measured directly. The protein is expressed mainly in cerebral cortex and hippocampus.

nodes.description: Hyperexcitable cortical networks generate the infantile-onset focal and generalized myoclonic seizures, the generalized tonic-clonic and febrile seizures, and the prolonged myoclonic attacks of FIME. FIME was described as an idiopathic epilepsy with no detectable brain lesion, interictal EEG is often normal despite frequent seizures, and in the founding family seizures persisted into adulthood.

nodes.description: TBC1D24 positively regulates the v-ATPase and is needed for normal presynaptic endocytosis and vesicle reacidification. Loss of TBC1D24 in mouse neurons impairs endocytosis, enlarges the endosomal compartment and reduces spontaneous neurotransmission. This mechanism is shared across the TBC1D24 spectrum and has not been measured specifically with the FIME alleles.
